_what: Desktop drag tests on the device-check list (Windows PC, 540x960 embedded game window = 270x480 game at 2x, emulate_touch_from_mouse = true, scroll_deadzone 6). Injected with game_eval: Input.parse_input_event() with InputEventMouseButton/InputEventMouseMotion carrying button_mask = LEFT and relative motion, one step per frame (a real mouse drag). godot-ai's input_mouse motion events carry no button mask or relative motion, so they only hover and cannot drag. Window coordinates; the game is at half scale.

tests.gesture: press on Row 03 at window (262,626), 12 steps of -16 px, release at (262,434)
tests.reading: A drag that starts on a STOP row does not scroll the list at all, and no row fires.
PASS rows let the ScrollContainer drag: the list follows the pointer 1:1 in game px, then coasts. The pressed row does not fire.

tests.gesture: press on Row 03, 4 steps of -8 window px (past the 6 px deadzone), release still over the same row
tests.reading: Once the ScrollContainer starts scrolling, the row's press is cancelled even when the release lands on the same row.

tests.gesture: tap (motion, press, release at the same point) on Row 03
tests.reading: PASS rows still fire on a plain tap.

tests.rows: PASS via the new Rows toggle (clicked with input_mouse)
tests.reading: The on-screen toggle switches every row to PASS; tapping it again shows 'Rows STOP' and mouse_filter 0.

conclusion_desktop_only: ARCHITECTURE 10.3 #7 / 18.1 #1 on desktop emulation: with default STOP buttons, a list made of buttons cannot be drag-scrolled at all (every drag starts on a button). PASS rows scroll, never fire on a drag, and still fire on a tap. The iPhone has to confirm this (AC-S02-13); the device check's 'Rows STOP/PASS' toggle lets the developer try both in one install.
